patch.value: GH-1631: expose bounded extension-owned diagnostics on expected SDK errors

GitHub report https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1631 requests a namespaced JSON-compatible extension diagnostics slot on PmCliErrorContext and createPmCliExpectedError. Its concrete producer is pm-changelog issue 302: selection_report loses structure through host-owned prose fields. Design typed SDK and CLI/TOON/JSON contracts with size bounds and explicit exclusion from telemetry/Sentry; avoid widening arbitrary error payload capture.

Cover public SDK typing and separately bundled expected errors; preserve nested safe JSON diagnostics in JSON and TOON; enforce bounded output and prove telemetry/Sentry exclusion with real local collectors; coordinate pm-changelog producer adoption in its own repository.
Extensions return actionable structured refusal facts through a documented namespaced SDK field, with deterministic budgets and no diagnostic payload entering telemetry or Sentry.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Implementation (branch fix/refusal-contract-precision):

- Contract: PmCliErrorContext gains an optional details slot typed PmCliErrorDetails (plain JSON: null, booleans, finite numbers, well-formed strings, arrays, plain objects). New core module src/core/shared/error-details.ts admits a value, returns a detached copy, and renders it whole within PM_CLI_ERROR_DETAILS_LIMITS (max_bytes 4096 of compact UTF-8 JSON, max_depth 8). Anything larger or malformed is replaced by a details_omitted receipt { reason, path?, byte_length?, byte_limit }. Partial structures are never emitted.
- SDK: createPmCliExpectedError validates details at construction and throws a TypeError naming the reason and path (unsupported_value, non_finite_number, malformed_unicode, reserved_key for __proto__, depth_limit, not_plain_object). Size is data-dependent, so it is bounded at render time, not refused. Exports from sdk and sdk/runtime: PM_CLI_ERROR_DETAILS_LIMITS, isPmCliErrorDetails, PmCliErrorDetails, PmCliErrorDetailValue, PmCliErrorDetailsOmission, PmCliErrorDetailsRejection.
- CLI: --json errors carry details or details_omitted (kept by --lean). Text output renders an indented TOON "Details:" block, which is the first collection the bounded text ladder drops. The telemetry classification is built without details.
- MCP: errorContent and writeError now recognize separately bundled expected errors by shape (they previously forwarded context only for instanceof PmCliError) and bound details the same way.
- Sentry: captured faults strip details from error_context, and beforeSend scrubs details from error-data contexts and extras.

Proof: tests/unit/core/shared/error-details.spec.ts (17 cases), error-guidance, MCP, Sentry helper/instrument and SDK index specs. tests/integration/telemetry/extension-error-provenance.spec.ts runs the built CLI under Node and Bun against real local OTLP and Sentry collectors: the probe extension's separately bundled refusal carries a marked details payload, the JSON refusal returns it whole, the text refusal renders the Details block, and the marker never appears in collected events, logs or telemetry.

Producer adoption (pm-changelog selection_report) belongs in the pm-changelog repository once a pm-cli release ships this slot. Filed there as the follow-up after merge.

patch.value: Extensions return structured refusal facts through a documented SDK field, bounded deterministically and never sent to telemetry or Sentry.

PmCliErrorContext.details with SDK admission (TypeError on malformed shapes), whole-or-receipt rendering within PM_CLI_ERROR_DETAILS_LIMITS in JSON, text and MCP, and exclusion from telemetry classification and Sentry payloads.

A separately bundled refusal's details reach JSON and text output whole under Node and Bun, oversized payloads become details_omitted receipts, and real local OTLP and Sentry collectors never receive the payload.
Expected SDK errors carry bounded, producer-owned structured diagnostics

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Codex review round 1 on PR #1649 (gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh). Five findings on this item, all verified and fixed:
- Nested Sentry payloads: console capture stores the error under extra.arguments and breadcrumbs, which the shallow scrub missed. omitEmbeddedPmCliErrorDetails now scrubs every embedded context/error_context in event extras, contexts and breadcrumbs (depth-bounded, cycle-safe, no getters run), in both beforeSend and beforeSendTransaction.
- Fault message leaking producer keys: createPmCliExpectedError's TypeError now names only the reason; the path sits on a non-enumerable path property.
- Amplification: shared array references could expand 10^8 leaves before the byte check. The walk now counts compact-JSON bytes as it goes and stops at the ceiling, so its cost is bounded by max_bytes (the test finishes in milliseconds). The receipt therefore no longer carries byte_length.
- Unbounded omission paths: capped at 160 UTF-8 bytes without splitting a character.
- Throwing details getters: accessors are refused without being run, at both the slot (CLI, MCP, telemetry omission) and inside values. Oversized well-formed details are kept as given and render as a byte_limit receipt.
New regression cases are in error-details, sdk-index, error-guidance, MCP and Sentry instrument specs.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Codex review round 2 on PR #1649: three findings on this item, all verified and fixed.
- CLI enrichment ran a separately bundled error's details getter: buildPmCliRecoveryContext spread the raw context. It now attaches recovery to a descriptor-preserving copy (frozen contexts included), so the renderer reports the getter as unsupported_value without running it. Covered in-process in error-handler-projection.spec.ts with a frozen, getter-carrying context.
- A root proxy whose getPrototypeOf trap throws escaped admission. The root shape check now runs inside the guarded walk.
- The typed-refusal fallback headline (pm-btv6x7 path) cut by UTF-16 units and could split an emoji. buildFallbackTitleFromMessage now cuts by code points.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
CodeRabbit full review on PR #1649 (head f7e12f69b): three new findings on this item, all fixed.
- Hostile proxy contexts and non-JSON members broke the MCP response. Foreign contexts are now read once as plain data by snapshotPmCliErrorContext (no getter runs, own enumerable data only, a details accessor becomes an unsupported_value receipt, an uninspectable context becomes {}), in both the CLI and MCP. MCP falls back to { code, context_unserializable: true } when JSON cannot encode the context.
- Oversized details stayed a live reference, so mutating them after construction could change the refusal. createPmCliExpectedError now records the host-set receipt details_omitted: { reason: "byte_limit", byte_limit } in place of details. PmCliErrorContext declares details_omitted as a host-owned field; renderers re-validate it, and telemetry omission removes it too, since its path can echo producer keys.
Its title-truncation, root-proxy and Unicode findings were already fixed in round 2.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Codex review round 3 on PR #1649: two findings on this item, both fixed.
- MCP ran custom toJSON hooks after bounding, so a context whose toJSON returned oversized details bypassed the ceiling, and a serializer that throws on a second call broke the response. MCP now serializes the snapshot exactly once and projects details on the plain result. A non-object result falls back to context_unserializable.
- Recorded details_omitted receipts were read through getters. Receipt fields are now read as own data descriptors, and accessor-backed fields are rejected without running.

value.text: CodeRabbit review of 6f3d87ab7 on PR #1649: createPmCliExpectedError with context: null threw from Object.hasOwn. null now means "no context" again, as it did before this change (regression case in sdk-index.spec.ts).

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 4 on PR #1649: MCP serialized the context before bounding diagnostics, so a nested getter inside details ran and shared trees were expanded. MCP now admits details from the snapshot with the bounded, getter-free walk first, then serializes only the remaining host fields once. A context-level toJSON is ignored, so it can neither replace nor expand the diagnostics. Regression cases cover a nested details getter (an unsupported_value receipt, the getter never runs), shared amplifying references (a byte_limit receipt) and a context toJSON (never invoked).

value.text: Codex review round 5 on PR #1649: isPmCliExpectedError threw when inspecting a revoked-proxy context (Array.isArray throws), so MCP errorContent threw instead of writing an error envelope. The predicate is now total and returns false for anything it cannot inspect, which also protects the CLI and Sentry paths. Covered in sdk-index and MCP specs.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 6 on PR #1649: omitPmCliErrorDetails and projectPmCliErrorContextDetails called Array.isArray outside their guards, so sentryCaptureCliError threw on a revoked-proxy context before captureException ran. Both checks now sit inside the guards, and the embedded-context scrubber skips nodes it cannot list. A captured fault with a revoked context reaches Sentry with error_context: {}.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Codex review round 7 on PR #1649: two findings, both fixed.
- Sentry's ExtraErrorData integration serializes an error's own context before beforeSend runs, so a context-level toJSON that copied details under another key (report.marker) survived the key-based scrub. Crash reports now carry an error context only through crashReportErrorContext: a getter-free snapshot reduced to top-level primitives, with no diagnostics, receipt or serializer. It is used for error_context and every embedded context, and beforeSend rebuilds the error-data entry from the original exception's own data property rather than from the serialized copy.
- A 20M-character string was JSON-encoded (about 120 MB) before the ceiling refused it. Admission now checks a constant-time lower bound (UTF-8 JSON needs at least one byte per UTF-16 unit, plus quotes) for every string value and key before scanning, encoding or building a path. A 20M-character value or key is refused in milliseconds.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Codex review round 8 on PR #1649: two findings, both fixed.
- Console-captured errors: Sentry normalizes console arguments and breadcrumbs (running custom toJSON hooks) before beforeSend, so a toJSON that flattened a diagnostic into a top-level primitive survived the primitive-only projection. Serialized embedded contexts whose originals cannot be recovered are now discarded (replaced with {}). Error-data entries are still rebuilt from the original exception, and the error_context extra our own capture produced is kept as its safe projection.
- A proxied diagnostics array could report a different length on each read (1, then NaN), which turned the byte count into NaN and disabled the ceiling. The length is now read once from its own descriptor and validated as a non-negative safe integer, and the ceiling check treats a non-finite count as exceeded.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Codex review round 9 on PR #1649: two findings, both fixed.
- A console-captured context whose toJSON returns a string was normalized into a string, which the object-only discard kept. Embedded context and error_context slots are now discarded whatever their serialized type, then only independently verified safe projections are restored (rebuilt error-data entries and our own error_context).
- Admitted details fit their 4,096-byte compact ceiling but can grow several times larger pretty-printed, so the generic diagnostic ladder dropped them from --json with only a generic omission entry. When details would push the pretty-printed envelope past the error diagnostic budget, they are now replaced up front with details_omitted: { reason: "diagnostic_budget", byte_limit }. PmCliErrorDetailsRejection gains that reason; the type is unreleased, and the SDK surface change is acknowledged.
